title: The 501 not_implemented envelope
description: The body every declared-but-unimplemented route answers with, in the error envelope of identity_cloudflare::error::ErrorEnvelope. The code is the one every layer agrees on: ApplicationError::NotImplemented and TransportError::Unimplemented both map to the string 'not_implemented', and docs/architecture/worker-architecture.md names ApplicationError::NotImplemented as the envelope for a declared route. The STATUS is 501 — deliberately OUTSIDE the closed HttpStatus set, because it is answered by a hand-built response at the route table rather than by ErrorEnvelope::status(). ErrorEnvelope::status() would map this code to 500, which is wrong for a declared route: a client that sees 500 retries, and a client that sees 501 stops.
x-rust-type: identity_cloudflare::error::ErrorEnvelope, built from a CloudflareError whose code() is "not_implemented"
x-serde-status: the envelope type is IMPLEMENTED; no Worker emits it yet — all three Worker composition roots are one-line placeholders (apps/*/worker/src/lib.rs), so in the repository as it stands no route is served at all. The 501 is CONTRACTED, not observed.

code.description: The stable machine-readable code. Present so a caller can tell 'this system has not built that yet' from 'you asked for the wrong thing' without reading the message.

message.description: The human-readable message. For a not-implemented failure the crate's own rendering is "this operation is not implemented yet (<operation>)" — UNIMPLEMENTED_MESSAGE plus the parenthesised operation name. It is client_safe, so this is the error's own text rather than the generic substitute. It never contains a secret and never claims a flow exists.
message.x-construction: identity_cloudflare::error::UNIMPLEMENTED_MESSAGE == "this operation is not implemented yet", rendered by CloudflareError::message_when_client_safe as format!("{UNIMPLEMENTED_MESSAGE} ({operation})")
message.test: identity_cloudflare::error::tests::an_unimplemented_error_says_so_in_the_message asserts the code, the presence of the operation name, and client_safe == true

request_id.description: The request identifier, when the transport had one, so a user can quote it and an operator can find the log line. OMITTED from the body entirely when absent, not serialised as null.
request_id.x-serde-note: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none", default)] — absent from the body, not null.

client_safe.description: Whether the message is the error's own text rather than the generic substitute. TRUE for not_implemented: TransportError::Unimplemented is client-safe, and a caller must be able to tell from the response body that the system has not built this yet without reading the code and inferring.

x-accepted-values.source: TransportError::is_client_safe — Unimplemented is not among the operator-facing variants
x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is a plain bool in Rust; the true value follows from which variant was constructed

x-do-not-confuse-with.why: the OAuth endpoints answer in the RFC 6749 section 5.2 shape because a third-party OAuth client library parses that one; the rest of the API answers in this shape because Ecoma's own clients parse it. One envelope for both would break one of them. A DEFERRED /oauth/* route in the bootstrap is contracted to answer THIS envelope, because the 501 comes from the route table before any OAuth-specific handler runs.
